title: Give the two destructive confirms a danger weight, not the primary one
body:
## Summary
"Yes, disconnect" (accounts) and "Yes, forget" (apps) are styled `btn--primary`, the same weight as Connect and Register; the design system's Button has no destructive variant.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/scenes/accounts/view.tsx Disconnect renders `<Button size="sm" variant="primary">Yes, disconnect</Button>` and apps/desktop/src/scenes/apps/view.tsx Forget renders `variant="primary"` for "Yes, forget". Both destroy something (the stored credential; the origin row with its switch and pinned classes). apps/desktop/src/components/Button.tsx:14 declares `Variant = "primary" | "secondary" | "ghost"`, so the scene cannot say "destructive" at all. The visual-craft rule: a destructive action styled identically to a benign one misstates its consequence. Fixed looks like a `danger` variant (a status-error token outline or fill) in components/Button and both confirms using it.

## Flow
- open an account -> Disconnect -> the confirm shows "Yes, disconnect" in the accent primary fill
- the same fill is Connect / Connect with Google / Register and open - the one-press creating acts
- build: add `danger` to Button's Variant and styles (components context), then switch both confirms; pin with a view test asserting `.btn--danger` on both

## Expected impact
A person confirming a destructive act sees it ranked as destructive. Risk: Button is shared by every surface; adding a variant changes none of them.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - the destructive confirm reads as destructive
Before: 2 of 2 destructive confirms use btn--primary; 0 danger variants exist
After: predicted 2 of 2 on a danger variant
Method: simulation - walked the two confirms and Button.tsx; the variant lives in components/ (another context), so it was not built here
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: view tests asserting `.btn--danger` on both confirms after a Button `danger` variant lands (components context owns Button)

title: Stop every apps orb floating forever on its own will-change layer
body:
## Summary
Every orb in the Apps field runs `orb-float` 6s infinite alternate with `will-change: transform`, so a settled field keeps one composited layer and one running animation per registered app.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/scenes/apps/apps.css:310-313 `.orb__float { animation: orb-float 6s ease-in-out infinite alternate; will-change: transform; }`, and the same AppOrb is drawn at 112px per app in the field and at 240px on the app level (apps/desktop/src/scenes/apps/view.tsx Field, AppLevel). README 3.1 / ADR 0089 say a settled scene asks for no frames; the motion technique taste-budgets ("an idle loop reads as loading though nothing runs") and performance-discipline ("idle profile shows clock wake-ups with nothing running") name this. The perf gate (scripts/perf-gate.mjs) counts idle rAF requests, which a CSS animation never makes, so `idleFrameRequests: 0` cannot see it. Fixed looks like the float on the hovered or focused orb only (or none), `will-change` dropped at rest, the reading spin kept since it carries meaning.

## Flow
- register 10 apps -> open the Apps field and leave it
- each orb's `g.orb__float` animates translateY 0 -> -3px forever; the compositor produces frames for the whole field
- build: move the float behind `.apps__orb:hover`/`:focus-visible`, drop will-change at rest; extend the perf drive to sample compositor frames over an idle second

## Expected impact
Idle GPU and battery cost on the Apps field falls to about nothing. Risk: the field reads more still; a design call on whether the float is wanted at rest.

## Evaluation
Claim: performance - a settled Apps field asks for no frames
Before: N infinite CSS animations and N will-change layers at rest for N registered apps (heavy fixture: every app)
After: 0 at rest (predicted)
Method: simulation - read from the CSS; the perf gate counts rAF only, so an idle compositor-frame probe is needed and was not built
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: perf:apps drive sampling compositor frames (e.g. CDP Performance.getMetrics or a trace) over an idle second on the heavy fixture, before and after

title: Say in the Apps scene when register, forget or the switch is refused
body:
## Summary
The Browser module's actions report a refused register, forget, switch or navigation only to console.error, so the Apps scene shows nothing when one fails, and Forget has already risen to the field.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/modules/browser/index.ts:59-83: `const report = (what) => (e) => console.error(...)`, and register / forget / setEnabled / navigate each end in `.catch(report(...))`. apps/desktop/src/scenes/apps/view.tsx Forget calls `actions.forget(app.origin); go({ root: "apps" })` before the forget resolves, and Register empties its box at the press. A refused forget leaves the app on the field with no word; a refused register leaves an empty box and no app. error-handler / observability: a failure path that leaves no trace a person can see.

## Flow
- make the origins write fail (daemon or store error) -> press Forget twice
- the depth rises to the field; the app is still there; nothing says the forget was refused
- build: the module keeps a per-origin `error` beside its actions (as the connectors store does with `errors`), the scene renders it on the field and the app level

## Expected impact
A refused act is said where it was asked for. Risk: the module's model gains a field; the old Browser view and the scene both read it.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - a refused register/forget/switch is visible
Before: 0 of 4 browser actions surface a refusal in the scene
After: 4 of 4 (predicted)
Method: simulation - read the module and the scene; the module is another context (modules/browser), so it was not built here
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: an interaction test with a rejecting forget/register action asserting a visible refusal on the field and the app level (out-of-scope seam: modules/browser)

title: Keep focus in the page band when a tab is closed from the strip
body:
## Summary
Closing a tab from the page band's strip unmounts its chip with the focused close button, so focus falls to the document, as the field's page chips did before this round.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/scenes/apps/strip.tsx TabStrip renders one `tab-chip` per tab with a `tab-chip__close` button that calls `onClose(tab.id)`; when `tabs:changed` drops the tab the chip and its focused button unmount. This round fixed the same loss for the field's page chips (apps/desktop/src/scenes/apps/view.tsx Field) and the allow-list's Remove; the strip is the third site. In the page shape the band sits over a native webview (ADR 0088) and closing the shown tab also moves the depth (apps/desktop/src/scenes/apps/live.tsx Band), so where focus should land (the next tab's chip, the address field) needs the real window to judge.

## Flow
- open three pages -> in the page shape, Tab to the second chip's close -> Enter
- the chip goes; document.activeElement is <body>
- build: remember the closed index, focus the close now in that place once the tab is gone, else the address field; pin in strip.test.tsx; check in the Tauri window that the webview does not take focus first

## Expected impact
A keyboard user closing several tabs keeps their place. Risk: focus moving inside the band while the webview swaps pages.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - focus survives a tab close in the band
Before: focus falls to <body> on every strip close (same mechanism as the field chips, red before this round's fix there)
After: focus on the next close (predicted)
Method: simulation - the jsdom instrument exists (strip.test.tsx), the native webview's focus behaviour does not exist in jsdom
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
apps/desktop/src/scenes/apps/strip.tsx (TabStrip)  <button type="button" className="tab-chip__close focus-ring" ... onClick={() => onClose(tab.id)}>
apps/desktop/src/scenes/apps/live.tsx (Band)  focus: (id) => { browser.actions.focus(id); ... useDepth.getState().go(pagePath(itemOfTab(tab))); }
instrument: a strip.test.tsx close-focus case plus one pass in the real Tauri window with a page webview shown

title: Tell a page the relay could not read apart from one that offers no tools
body:
## Summary
The app level says "This page offers no tools of its own" for every answered-empty page, including one whose bridge request failed for a reason other than a timeout, while the strip over the same page says "no bridge" with the reason.

## Description
apps/desktop/src/scenes/apps/model.ts ToolSources.byTab carries `{ tools, asking }` only; the store's TabTools carries `problem` (apps/desktop/src/stores/tools.ts:41, "`timeout` here means this page has no tools", ADR 0008). selectApps turns any settled entry into `answered: true` with its tools, so apps/desktop/src/scenes/apps/view.tsx ToolList renders the no-tools sentence for an IPC failure (`String(e)`, stores/tools.ts:91) exactly as for a page with no bridge. The strip (apps/desktop/src/scenes/apps/strip.tsx ToolCount) shows any problem as a warning badge with the reason. Fixed looks like AppTools carrying `problem`, the app level saying the reason verbatim for a non-timeout problem and keeping the generic-hands sentence for a timeout.

## Flow
- open a page whose bridge_list fails with an IPC error -> open its app level
- "What the page offers" says it offers no tools of its own; the band above says "no bridge" with the error
- build: add `problem` to ToolSources/AppTools, carry it in selectApps, render it in ToolList; model.test and view.test cases for timeout vs failure

## Expected impact
A broken relay is not presented as an ordinary tool-less site. Risk: the timeout wording must stay as ADR 0008 has it.

## Evaluation
Claim: user - a failure renders differently from an empty answer
Before: 1 rendering for 2 states (no tools, relay failed)
After: 2 renderings (predicted)
Method: simulation - walked selectApps and ToolList with a failed entry; which problems besides `timeout` occur in practice needs the relay's error vocabulary
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: model.test and view.test cases with a byTab entry carrying problem `timeout` and problem `bridge unavailable`, asserting two different sentences

title: Cover the Apps live wiring: labelOf, the band's focus move and onShown
body:
## Summary
apps/desktop/src/scenes/apps/live.tsx has no test: the breadcrumb labeller, the band's focus override that moves the depth with the tab, and the onShown move to a page are each unpinned.

## Description
`grep -rl "scenes/apps/live\|from \"./live\"" src --include=*.test.*` finds no test importing it (only modules/voice/live.test.ts, unrelated). labelOf is pure (`Page` for the page shape, the tool name, else itemLabel); Band wraps `actions.focus` so a tab change calls `useDepth.getState().go(pagePath(itemOfTab(tab)))`; useAppsModel passes `onShown: (origin) => go(pagePath(origin))`. A regression in any of these changes what the crumbs say or leaves the depth on the old page while the webview shows another, and no gate sees it.

## Flow
- write live.test.tsx: labelOf over the fixtures for the field, an app, a page and a tool
- render Band with mocked useBrowserModel and useDepth; press a tab chip; assert depth.go(pagePath(item))
- render Live with a mocked module hook; fire onShown; assert go(pagePath(origin))

## Expected impact
The page shape's crumbs and depth sync are pinned. Risk: none; tests only.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - live wiring under a gate
Before: 0 tests import scenes/apps/live.tsx
After: 3 behaviours pinned (predicted)
Method: simulation - the grep is the Before; the store mocks were not built this round
Result: better
Gate: none
